name: PowerAccent (Quick Accent)
note: P0/P1/P2 capability spec grounded in distilled_v2/microsoft-PowerToys/PowerAccent.md (feature->file map + regression history). Executed against REAL freshly-built binaries. The end-user overlay-summon path (hold letter + activation key) is BLOCKED in this session by synthetic-input denial (see report.md section a); these checks exercise the same behavioral surface that FEEDS the overlay (candidate data, glyph correctness, native/managed enum lockstep, DPI/caret positioning) plus the module launch/enable/exit lifecycle.

checks.description: Holding an accent-capable letter yields a non-empty candidate list; unmapped keys / no languages yield nothing (the data the overlay renders).
French 'a' overlay shows exactly [a-grave, a-circumflex, a-acute, a-diaeresis, a-tilde, ae] in order.
French 'e' overlay shows exactly [e-acute, e-grave, e-circumflex, e-diaeresis, euro] in order.
French 'c' overlay shows exactly [c-cedilla].
Enabling Quick Accent launches PowerToys.PowerAccent.exe, which stays resident and materializes its settings (module initialized).
When multiple selected languages map the same glyph, the overlay shows it once (no duplicate candidates).
Candidates are ordered by language DisplayOrder; a single selected language yields only that language's glyphs.
'ALL' language setting expands to every language exactly once and returns a stable cached union.
The managed LetterKey enum stays in lockstep (names + values) with the native WinRT keyboard-hook enum, so the right key triggers the right candidates.
Every language entry is well-formed (non-empty id, non-null glyphs, present in display/group order maps) so the language picker and overlay never break.
Spoken languages are listed alphabetically by display name in the settings language picker.
An unknown/unsupported language identifier fails fast instead of returning silent-wrong candidates.
Currency-only language maps 'e' to exactly the euro sign.
With all languages enabled, 'a' candidates include the common Latin accents (a-grave/acute/circumflex/diaeresis/tilde).
A second Quick Accent instance detects the 'QuickAccent' mutex and exits, leaving exactly one resident owner of the keyboard hook.
Disabling Quick Accent signals POWERACCENT_EXIT_EVENT and the process shuts down cleanly (uninstalls the global hook).
At 100% DPI the overlay anchors (TopLeft..BottomRight/Center) land at the expected screen coordinates.
At 150% DPI the overlay footprint scales so it stays on-screen at high-DPI.
The overlay honors the active monitor's origin (including offset and negative-origin monitors).
In caret-follow mode the overlay centers above the caret, clamps at screen edges, and flips below when there's no room above.
